issues.source_quote: Как говорит наш дорогой шеф, в нашем деле гланое - этот самый реализм!
issues.translation_quote: Ha-ha-ha-ha-ha-ha-ha! Well! Time to go, tourist! No need... Go on...
issues.justification: Surrounding lines are fine, but the fake-injury scene's comic logic is blurred: 'Нынадо' (a mock-Georgian/dialect 'don't need to') is rendered as a flat 'No need...' losing the characteristic comic voice of Lyolik's speech.

issues.source_quote: Упал, выругался... Чёрт возьми! Ух, прости, "Чёрт побери!" Смотри, не перепутай!
issues.translation_quote: You fall, you swear... "God damn it!" Oh, sorry: "Damn it!"
issues.justification: The joke is that the password is the exact phrase 'Чёрт побери' and the wrong variant must not be used. 'God damn it' vs 'Damn it' loses the near-synonym confusion and adds a religious oath absent from the source.

issues.source_quote: Вы тоже здесь едете?
issues.translation_quote: Are you staying here too?
issues.justification: 'Едете' means traveling; 'staying' mistranslates the idea of sharing the cabin on the voyage.

issues.source_quote: Мы вообще дальше Дубровки никуда не ездили. - Х-х-х-х-ха... Но и Вы, тоже едете за границу в первый раз? Нет, я никуда не еду. Мы провожаем папу!!!
issues.translation_quote: - Ha-ha-ha! And is this your first trip abroad too? No, I'm not going anywhere. We're seeing Daddy off!
issues.justification: The scene is a staged radio rehearsal gag, but the interviewer's question and the child's interruption are muddled; speaker turns are unclear and the humor of the interruption is weakened.

issues.source_quote: Фрис-стрит, рыбна улица, - Аптека «Чиканук»...
issues.translation_quote: Fris Street, Fish Street, - The Chikanuk pharmacy...
issues.justification: The mock-foreign 'рыбна улица' (broken Russian-like foreign speech, spy-contact phrase) is rendered as plain English 'Fish Street', losing the comic foreign-accent effect.

issues.source_quote: Нет, с ночёвкой не поеду, боюсь застудить.
issues.translation_quote: No, I can't stay overnight. I might catch a chill.
issues.justification: Minor meaning shift, but more importantly 'Козлодоев' wordplay: the source insults Kozadoyev's name as 'Козлодоев' (козёл + доить), and the translation retains the names but does not convey that the pun is deliberate insult.

issues.source_quote: Козлодоев... Козадоев! Казладоев!
issues.translation_quote: Kozlodoyev... Kozodoyev! Kozlodoyev!
issues.justification: The source name is 'Козадоев' (Kozadoyev) and Lyolik's slip is 'Козлодоев'. The translation renders the correct name inconsistently as 'Kozodoyev' earlier ('Kozodoyev') and 'Kozlodoyev', scrambling the joke on mispronounced names; the third variant 'Казладоев' is also collapsed to the same as the first.

issues.source_quote: Чтоб ты исдох! Чтоб я видел тебя у гробу, у белых тапках!
issues.translation_quote: Drop dead! I hope I see you in your coffin wearing white slippers!
issues.justification: The source is deliberately nonstandard, Odessa-flavored speech ('исдох', 'у гробу, у белых тапках'). The translation is standard English and loses the colorful dialect that characterizes the neighbor.

issues.source_quote: Собака - друг человека! ... Управдом - друг человека!
issues.translation_quote: But here, the building manager is man's best friend!
issues.justification: Acceptable literal rendering, but 'Вы ... Лондон' retort: the sharp, ironic reversal is okay; however 'Your 'private apartment' remark ('Вам предоставлена отдельная квартира') loses the sarcasm.

issues.source_quote: Измене!
issues.translation_quote: Treason!
issues.justification: Nadya accuses Senya of 'измена', which in this context means marital infidelity (and ambiguously treason). Rendering only as 'Treason' loses the double reading that drives the comic misunderstanding.

issues.source_quote: Эти игрушки идиотские!
issues.translation_quote: Those idiotic toys!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the key joke 'Дичь' (game/wild fowl as code word and the 'Операция Дичь') is explained with inconsistent rendering 'Operation Game' and 'What? "Game"!', which garbles Lyolik's explanation that the code name is 'Дичь' and the restaurant detail.

issues.source_quote: Не взял попутных - это не таксист!
issues.translation_quote: He won't take passengers? He's no taxi driver!
issues.justification: The line is Gorbunkov's inner paranoia that the driver refused to pick up passersby, so he's 'not a real cabbie'. The translation turns it into a question and breaks the logic of Senya's suspicion.

issues.source_quote: Эти кретины уверяли, что он был без сознания...
issues.translation_quote: Those idiots swore he was unconscious...
issues.justification: 'Кретины' is stronger than 'idiots' for the repeated 'идиот' motif, causing no distinction between registers; minor.

issues.source_quote: Хорошо бы ай-лю-лю, цигель, цигель - время, товарищ!
issues.translation_quote: "ai-lyulyu" would be lovely, but tsigel, tsigel: time!
issues.justification: 'Цигель, цигель, ай-люлю' is a famous nonsense refrain which the guide mimics; leaving it transliterated without any comic cue leaves English viewers without the joke that this is a parody of foreign flirting.

issues.source_quote: Ну что Вы так, Семён Семёнович... Спокойно… Выпейте! Я не пью... Читали в «Неделе», отдел для, дома для семьи...
issues.translation_quote: I read it in Nedelya, in the home-and-family section.
issues.justification: The captain says 'You've read' (Читали...) as a persuasion; the translation attributes reading to the speaker, and 'Nedelya' is left unexplained.

issues.source_quote: Не положено, инструкция!
issues.translation_quote: Not allowed. Regulations!
issues.justification: Acceptable, but the stiff bureaucratic tone is only moderately conveyed.

issues.source_quote: Такова «сё ля ви», как говорят у них...
issues.translation_quote: C'est la vie, as they say over here...
issues.justification: 'У них' means 'over there/in their country' (abroad); 'over here' reverses the deictic and mistranslates the speaker's location.

issues.source_quote: Как говорит наш любимый шеф, если человек идиот - то это надолго.
issues.translation_quote: As our beloved Chief says, if a man's an idiot, it's for life.
issues.justification: Acceptable; however 'Куда поедем? Домой.' etc. are fine. This item is fine in meaning but the later 'Как говорит наш дорогой шеф, нет такого мужа...' is fine too; the issue is the loss of the running gag structure where the Chief's aphorisms are comic misquotes.

issues.source_quote: Идиот! Дитям - мороженое! О-о! Ах глаз - ерунда, пройдёт!
issues.translation_quote: Idiot! Ice cream for the kids! Oh! My eye? It's nothing. It'll heal!
issues.justification: 'Дитям' is a deliberately folksy/uneducated form and the line is Gesha's reaction to being hit in the eye by the kid's ice cream; the translation does not make clear what happened and loses the slapstick.

issues.source_quote: Пьянству - бой!
issues.translation_quote: Down with drunkenness!
issues.justification: Acceptable rendering of the Soviet slogan, but without cultural flavor.

issues.source_quote: Получил премию. А по протоколу, за одно зеркальное разбитое стекло Ваш муж заплатил 97 рублей 18 копеек!
issues.translation_quote: His friend got a bonus and invited him. According to the report, your husband paid 97 rubles and 18 kopecks for a single plate-glass window he broke!
issues.justification: Acceptable; but 'Шампанское по утрам пьют или аристократы, или дегенераты!' is fine. Main issue: the ambiguity of 'Его товарищ пригласил' is fine; the line is near-correct.

issues.source_quote: Достаточно одной таблэтки...
issues.translation_quote: One tablet is enough...
issues.justification: Ok, but the following exchange 'Скажите, пожалуйста, У Вас нет такого же, но без крыльев?' is a comedic scene in a department store; the translation also contains stray subtitle timing text '1107 01:12:00,413 --> 01:12:01,513' inserted in the output, which is an addition not in the source.

issues.source_quote: Печёнкой чую, клюнула настоящая рыба.
issues.translation_quote: My gut tells me this is a real catch.
issues.justification: Acceptable. However 'Психическое...' ('The psychological one') is fine. The flagged issue is 'Дайте-ка записку! Французские, "Шанель, номер пять"' rendered as 'Let me see that note! French perfume.' — it omits that the note lists the perfume to buy, losing the comedic reading.

issues.source_quote: Не беспокойся, алкаш, не сорвёшь!
issues.translation_quote: Don't worry, you drunk. You won't pull it down!
issues.justification: The cast was attached by Lyolik's gang; the line is about the false cast being firmly fixed ('you won't tear it off'). Rendering as 'pull it down' is unclear and loses the double meaning.

issues.source_quote: Я встретил Вас и всё былое В отжившем сердце ожило...
issues.translation_quote: I met you, and the memories Stirred in my weary heart...
issues.justification: The final line repeats the romance 'Я встретил вас' as a closing; here the translation also appends an extra repeated line at the very end ('I met you, and the memories stirred in my weary heart...') that is not in the source, an addition.

issues.source_quote: Такси? Говорит Семён Семёнович Горбунков.
issues.translation_quote: Taxi service? This is Semyon Semyonovich Gorbunkov.
issues.justification: The song lyrics throughout are heavily adapted: 'Остров Невезения' rhyme and 'Трынь-трава' (a Russian idiom meaning 'I don't care') are rendered as 'who-cares grass', which is an awkward invention that loses the idiom and the folk-magical grass reference.

issues.source_quote: Если мы Вам будем нужны… Я вызываю такси на своё имя.
issues.translation_quote: If you need us... I'll call a taxi in my name.
issues.justification: The source says the colonel will call a taxi 'on his own name' as a signal; the translation reverses the role (it should be Senya calling a taxi). Combined with the earlier line it confuses the contact protocol.

issues.source_quote: Хорошо Вы поёте!
issues.translation_quote: You sing well!
issues.justification: Neutral; the flirt/humor in the interrogation scene is slightly flattened.
